answer: In a proof-of-space protocol, each agent must commit verifiable hard drive sectors to anchor its identity on a shared ledger. Gateways enforce a velvet rope admission filter to block transient sybils that appear and vanish like a comet. An attacker incurs the scarce, verifiable cost of dedicated physical disk capacity and read-write endurance per identity. A key limitation is that large data centers can repurpose idle drive arrays to generate excess identities at near-zero marginal cost.
